requirements.requirement: Configure node1 to route between lan-a (node2) and lan-b (node3) so they can reach each other directly on any port, preserving original source addresses
requirements.summary: VyOS node1 was given addresses on both LAN interfaces (eth1=10.10.1.254/24, eth2=10.10.2.254/24) and a forwarding firewall rule with default-action accept (no NAT rules were configured), with ip_forward=1 confirmed. End-to-end ICMP ping and a TCP payload over port 5201 both succeeded between node2 (10.10.1.10) and node3 (10.10.2.10). A tcpdump capture taken directly on node3's LAN interface shows the ICMP traffic arriving with source IP 10.10.1.10 unchanged, directly demonstrating no source address translation. Because the router policy is protocol/port-agnostic (stateless forward-accept, no NAT), this evidence generalizes to arbitrary ports, not just the specific ports tested.

requirements.requirement: Implement the routing configuration using Ansible
requirements.summary: An Ansible project (inventory.ini, playbook.yml, templates/) was created on node4, the designated control_node, and ansible-playbook was run from there to configure node1 (VyOS interface addressing + firewall) and node2/node3 (systemd-networkd LAN addressing + static routes). The playbook was re-run successfully (idempotent, no failures) both mid-task and after all four node reboots.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (node1-node4), each showing pre-restart healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and recovered state
requirements.summary: For all four nodes, a pre-restart boot_id was captured, a reboot was triggered, the node went unreachable for a bounded interval, and a distinct post-restart boot_id was observed (node1: 9028a473->f2d3512e; node2: e4e401d2->f4198708; node3: fa1e87e6->5424ec17; node4: a6937a34->7df4172c), matching the fixed lifecycle before/after-executor boot-identity snapshots. Post-restart recovery was directly verified: node1's VyOS interface addresses/firewall rule and ip_forward persisted, node2/node3's systemd-networkd LAN files and routes persisted, and node2->node3 ping succeeded again; node4's Ansible project persisted and a fresh playbook run against all nodes completed successfully, confirming cluster-wide recovered state.

overall_summary: The executor successfully configured node1 as a VyOS router with addressed LAN interfaces and a default-accept forwarding firewall rule (no NAT), and directly demonstrated bidirectional node2<->node3 reachability with original source addresses preserved via a tcpdump capture on node3. The implementation was done entirely via an Ansible playbook run from the designated control node (node4), including a working solution to Ubuntu 16.04's Python incompatibility with modern ansible-core. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was executed on all four nodes with clear pre-restart baselines, restart acknowledgements, changed boot identities, and directly observed recovery of VyOS config, LAN addressing/routes, and end-to-end connectivity, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Minor hygiene issues (a stale root authorized_keys entry on node1 and a leftover temp script) were not cleaned up but pose low risk and don't affect task functionality.
limitations: The TCP 'any port' claim rests on a single tested TCP port (5201) plus ICMP; source-address preservation was captured via tcpdump only for the ICMP traffic, not the TCP session, though the router's stateless accept-all/no-NAT policy makes this evidence reasonably generalizable.
No test of UDP traffic or high-numbered ephemeral source ports was captured, though the routing policy is port/protocol-agnostic.

The residual root authorized_keys entry on node1 was not confirmed to be non-functional beyond the executor's own troubleshooting observations (PermitRootLogin effective value came from /run/sshd/sshd_config, a runtime-generated file, which is credible but not independently re-verified at the end of the session).

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map cleanly to bootstrapping SSH access, applying the routing config, collecting bounded verification evidence, and the restart protocol; transient nc listener/tcpdump artifacts on node3 were properly cleaned up (cmd-ef364f65445741e3). However, two unnecessary/residual mutations remain: (1) an early troubleshooting step appended the cluster SSH public key to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys on node1 (cmd-641f2dc8eed74e61) before the executor discovered VyOS's root-login restriction and pivoted to the 'vyos' user; this root authorized_keys entry was never used again and was not removed, leaving a stale credential-relevant residue on the router node. (2) The rendered VyOS configuration script /tmp/vyos_lan_routing.sh was left on node1 after use (visible in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot) rather than cleaned up. Both are low-risk/bounded (no destructive or broad changes, no weakened security posture given root pubkey login was independently confirmed disabled), but they are retained residue rather than fully reverted.
